summary: @servicetitan/carto-charts-react ships install-time alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub, extracts and chmods it executable in a temp directory, then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'], { stdio: 'inherit' })` to run a sibling 727KB single-line obfuscated JavaScript file. `math_init.js` uses a rotated string-array loader (`WV8StW` rotator, `n7gIxM` numeric/string array, `_0xNNNN` mangled identifiers) — an obfuscator.io-style packed payload. Fetching a second language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling on `npm install` is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-based scanners: the executing bytes are never parsed by Node tooling. The behavior is unrelated to the package's stated purpose (a React chart wrapper), and the `@servicetitan/*` scope suggests namespace abuse or dependency-confusion targeting ServiceTitan builds.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
